name: Dubstep / UK 140
summary: Halfstep frame: kick on 1, one snare or rim on 3, never a 2-and-4 backbeat. The space between the anchors is the instrument — syncopated late kicks with garage-inherited swing, rims, shakers, tambourines and congas instead of busy hats, and odd-grid 32nd details kept toward the end of the bar.

sounds.kick: Raw, hollow 808-style kick with deep low end, overdriven and sent to echo/reverb, single-voice so tails never overlap.
sounds.snare: Layered electronic snare (160–200 Hz body) with a high-passed reverb clap, or a 707/808 snare for the minimal lane; rim shots carry beat 3 in the stripped tracks.
sounds.hats: Short gated maracas or closed hats punctuating the space, often pausing on beat 3; open hats only in the wobble-era stomp.
sounds.percussion: Acoustic shaker, two-pitch tambourine, cajón/congas high-passed at ~100 Hz, dub-delayed rims.
sounds.cymbals: Almost none; a dub-siren or reverse crash does the section work.

machines: Roland TR-808 — the kick and snare of DMZ-era halfstep (owned)
Roland TR-909 — clap layer under the snare (owned)
Akai MPC / S900 — sampled acoustic percussion with 12-bit weight (owned)
Native Instruments Battery / Reason Redrum — Mala's drum hosts (get elsewhere)
Acoustic percussion libraries — cajón, shaker, tambourine (get elsewhere)
